title: Cloud Application Security & Message Trace
description: Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Office 365 (splunk_ta_o365) -- two unrelated sourcetype families bundled together in the source dictionary: Cloud Application Security (Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps / MCAS), sourcetype o365:cas:api, with 5 content types (Alerts, Policies, Cloud Discovery, Entities, Files); and Message Trace, which uses one of two sourcetypes depending on cloud (o365:graph:messagetrace worldwide, o365:reporting:messagetrace for USGovGCC/USGovGCCHigh) but shares one common field set. As with o365:management:activity and the usage-reports schema, the source dictionary names no single reliable field that discriminates between the 5 CAS content types sharing o365:cas:api -- its own search tip groups by 'source' alone. The root schema is therefore a permissive catch-all for o365:cas:api plus the cleanly-discriminated messageTraceEvent branch; the 5 CAS content-type shapes are individually addressable *Event definitions under $defs. Property names use the '[]' suffix convention from the source dictionary's own Alerts section (e.g. 'entities[]') to identify array fields, and are only asserted where the dictionary gives a clear identifier-like token rather than a full descriptive phrase -- purely descriptive bullets (e.g. 'Cloud apps involved, countries, IP categories') are captured in each definition's description text instead of being turned into invented property keys.

o365CasApiEvent.description: Catch-all for the o365:cas:api sourcetype, shared by all 5 Cloud Application Security content types. See the individually addressable *Event definitions in this file's $defs for each content type's own documented fields -- this root-level branch does not attempt to discriminate between them since the source dictionary names no single reliable field for that.

source.description: Splunk source field -- the dictionary's own validation search groups by this.

alertEvent.description: Cloud Application Security Alerts -- risks and policy matches identified by Defender for Cloud Apps. Sourcetype o365:cas:api. Status: Active. CIM: Alerts. 'Cloud apps involved, countries, IP categories (Risky, Anonymous, etc.)' are documented conceptually but not as exact field names, so they are not asserted as properties here.

status.description: e.g. Open, Dismissed, Resolved, etc. -- not an exhaustive enum.

policyEvent.description: Cloud Application Security Policies -- threat protection / activity / file / OAuth / discovery policies. Sourcetype o365:cas:api. Status: Active. 'Filters / conditions' and 'Alert settings / daily alert limit' are documented conceptually but not as exact field names, so they are not asserted as properties here.

policyType.description: e.g. Activity, File, OAuth App, Anomaly Detection, App Discovery, etc. -- not an exhaustive enum.

governanceActions.description: e.g. notify, suspend user, revoke OAuth, quarantine file, etc. -- not an exhaustive enum.

cloudDiscoveryEvent.description: Cloud Application Security Cloud Discovery -- discovered cloud apps, traffic, users. Sourcetype o365:cas:api. Status: Deprecated -- Microsoft removed the discovery API endpoint. Disable this content type to avoid errors; use alternative discovery methods or Event Hub if still required. The source dictionary gives no field-level detail for this content type, so no properties are asserted beyond 'sourcetype'.

entityEvent.description: Cloud Application Security Entities -- users, accounts, IP addresses, devices, etc. Sourcetype o365:cas:api. Status: Active. Fields vary by entity type (user, account, IP, device, app...). 'Affiliated cloud apps' is documented conceptually but not as an exact field name; a best-effort affiliatedCloudApps array property is still included since it reads as a clear compound concept rather than a vaguer descriptive phrase.

fileEvent.description: Cloud Application Security Files -- files and folders metadata in connected apps. Sourcetype o365:cas:api. Status: Active (file monitoring must be enabled).

app.description: Service where the file resides, e.g. OneDrive, SharePoint, Box, etc.

messageTraceEvent.description: Message Trace. Two sourcetypes sharing one common field set: o365:graph:messagetrace (Worldwide, via the Microsoft Graph Message Trace API, lookback up to 90 days) and o365:reporting:messagetrace (USGovGCC/USGovGCCHigh, via the Exchange Online Reporting Web Service, lookback up to 10 days). CIM: Email (strong mapping for recipient, src_user, status, size, message_id, etc.). Permission: ExchangeMessageTrace.Read.All (Worldwide); Gov clouds use the Reporting Web Service path instead. 'Detailed timestamps and descriptions per hop' (an additional/expanded Graph detail) is documented conceptually but not as an exact field name.

Status.description: e.g. Delivered, Failed, Pending, Expanded, Quarantined, FilteredAsSpam, etc. -- not an exhaustive enum.

eventActions.description: Event-level actions when expanded, e.g. Receive, Deliver, Fail, Defer, etc. -- not an exhaustive enum.
